record.title: Polynomial-time fixed-topology minimum-bead tree conjecture
record.statement: Let $N$ be a set of terminals embedded in the Euclidean plane, and let $G$ be any tree topology on $N$ whose Steiner points have degree at least three. **Fixed-topology bead-minimization conjecture.** Finding a tree $T$ on $N$ with the same topology as $G$ and minimizing $\mathrm{beads}(T)$ can be done in polynomial time. This conjecture is motivated by the prospect of a polynomial-time algorithm based on displacing Steiner points of a Steiner minimum tree; the supplied text gives no resolution.
record.source_name: M. Brazil, C. J. Ras and D. A. Thomas, “Approximating Minimum Steiner Point Trees in Minkowski Planes”, arXiv:1307.2987 (2013).

record.title: Complex almost-injective intensity measurements have NP-complete consistency
record.statement: Let $\mathcal{F}=\{\Phi_M\}_{M=2}^\infty$ be a family of ensembles $\Phi_M=\{\varphi_{M;n}\}_{n=1}^{2M}\subseteq\mathbb{C}^M$ which yield **almost injective intensity measurements** and have complex rational entries that can be computed in polynomial time. **The consistency conjecture.** Then $\textsc{ConsistentIntensities}[\mathcal{F}]$ is $\NP$-complete. This would strengthen the preceding hardness result for the smallest possible almost-injective ensembles in the complex case, paralleling the established result for full spark ensembles with $M+1$ measurements; the conjectured NP-completeness is not resolved in the supplied text.

record.title: The planar-graph decontamination-time conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a planar graph on $n$ vertices. The decontamination time $\tau(G)$ is the minimum number of agents needed to decontaminate $G$.

**Planar-graph decontamination-time conjecture.** Any planar graph $G$ on $n$ vertices can be decontaminated with

$$
\tau(G)=O(\sqrt{n}).
$$

The paper proves an $O(\sqrt{n})$ upper bound for trees and gives planar graphs whose immunity number is greater than $\frac{\sqrt{n}}{2}$, so the conjectured planar bound would be asymptotically tight up to constants. The source presents this as an open question.

record.title: The quasi-positivity and sharp HOMFLY bound conjecture for fillable knots
record.statement:
Let $K$ be a smooth knot type. The HOMFLY bound on the maximum Thurston–Bennequin number of $K$ is the upper bound obtained from the HOMFLY polynomial, and $K$ is **fillable** if it admits a Lagrangian filling. **Fillability conjecture.** A smooth knot type $K$ is fillable if and only if it is quasi-positive and the HOMFLY bound on the maximum Thurston–Bennequin number of $K$ is sharp.

This conjecture seeks a necessary and sufficient characterization of Lagrangian fillability using the known necessary condition of quasi-positivity together with sharpness of the HOMFLY bound. The paper establishes that all positive knots are fillable and that strong quasi-positivity alone does not characterize fillability, but the proposed equivalence remains open.

record.title: Tree-degree conjecture for S-Roth joins
record.statement:
Let $S$ be the independent set of $s$ vertices in $H$, let $G$ be a graph on the remaining $t$ vertices, and let $\overline{K}_{s} \vee G$ denote the join of $\overline{K}_{s}$ and $G$. Write $\Delta(G)$ for the maximum degree of $G$. A graph is **S-Roth** when its smallest signless Laplacian eigenvector has the prescribed sign pattern associated with $S$.

**Tree-degree conjecture.** Let $t>s \geq 6$ and let $H=\overline{K}_{s} \vee G$. If $G$ is a tree and if $\Delta(G) \leq s$, then $H$ is $S$-Roth.

This conjecture is inspired by the degree-two result and supported by extensive empirical evidence. The suggested approach uses inverses of matrices associated with trees, but the analysis is technically difficult even for paths and remains open for general trees.
record.source_name: Felix Goldberg and Steve Kirkland, “On the sign patterns of the smallest signless Laplacian eigenvector”, arXiv:1307.7749 (2013).

record.title: Strict maximum-degree conjecture for S-Roth joins
record.statement:
Let $S$ be the independent set of $s$ vertices in $H$, let $G$ be a graph on the remaining $t$ vertices, and let $\overline{K}_{s} \vee G$ denote the join of $\overline{K}_{s}$ and $G$. Write $\Delta(G)$ for the maximum degree of $G$. A graph is **S-Roth** when its smallest signless Laplacian eigenvector has the prescribed sign pattern associated with $S$.

**Strict maximum-degree conjecture.** Let $t>s \geq 6$ and let $H=\overline{K}_{s} \vee G$. If $\Delta(G)<s$, then $H$ is $S$-Roth.

This is presented as a stronger conjecture than the tree-degree claim and has been verified computationally for values of $t$ up to $8$. Its general validity remains open.

record.title: Grant's total-degree conjecture for anti-directed Hamiltonian cycles
record.statement:
Let $D$ be a directed graph on $2n$ vertices, and let $\delta(D)$ denote its minimum total degree. **Grant's conjecture.** If

$$
\delta(D)\geq 2n+1,
$$

then $D$ contains an anti-directed Hamiltonian cycle. This modifies Grant's original conjecture after the semi-degree threshold was determined; the paper's main theorem shows that minimum semi-degree at least $n$ suffices apart from two extremal examples, while the total-degree formulation remains open.

record.title: Conjecture on semi-degree thresholds for non-anti-directed cycle orientations
record.statement:
Let $D$ be a directed graph on $n$ vertices, and let $\vec C$ be an orientation of a cycle on $n$ vertices that is not anti-directed. **Non-anti-directed cycle conjecture.** If

$$
\delta^0(D)\geq \frac{n}{2},
$$

then $\vec C\subseteq D$. Together with the paper's main theorem, this would give a full generalization of Dirac's theorem to directed graphs with respect to minimum semi-degree. The conjecture is presented as open in the source.

record.title: The bipartite-complement conjecture for extremal edge polytopes
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite simple graph in $\Omega_d$ attaining the maximum number of edges of its edge polytope, so that $\mu_d=\varepsilon(G)$.

**Bipartite-complement conjecture.** The complement of $G$ is a bipartite graph.

This conjecture proposes a structural description of graphs maximizing the number of edges of an edge polytope. The preceding theorem shows that complete graphs are extremal for $3\leq d\leq13$, while for $d\geq15$ some graphs have more edge-polytope edges than the complete graph; determining the exact maximum and an extremal graph remains unsolved for $d\geq15$.
record.source_name: Takayuki Hibi, Aki Mori, Hidefumi Ohsugi and Akihiro Shikama, “The number of edges of the edge polytope of a finite simple graph”, arXiv:1308.3530 (2016).

record.title: Exact-spectrum conjecture for interval colorings of K_{1,m,n}
record.statement:
Let $K_{1,m,n}$ be the complete tripartite graph with part sizes $1,m,n$, and let an interval $t$-coloring mean an interval edge-coloring using the colors $1,\ldots,t$. **Exact-spectrum conjecture.** Graph $K_{1,m,n}$ has an interval $t$-coloring if and only if

$$
t=m+n\quad\text{and}\quad \gcd(m+1,n+1)=1.
$$

This is posed as a future-work conjecture about the exact number of colors. The source proves non-colorability when the gcd exceeds $1$, but does not resolve the full assertion.

record.title: Non-isomorphic graphs with the same subtree polynomial
record.statement:
Let $n$ be a positive integer, and let the subtree polynomial of a graph $G$ be

$$
s_G(x)=\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}a_kx^k,
$$

where $a_k$ counts the subtrees with $k$ edges. **Subtree-polynomial multiplicity conjecture.** For any $n$, one can construct $n$ pairwise non-isomorphic graphs that all share the same subtree polynomial. The paper motivates this by pigeonhole considerations, since there should be many more graphs on $n$ vertices than possible subtree polynomials, but gives no resolution in the supplied text.

record.title: The nef Cartier b-divisor determination conjecture
record.statement:
Let $X$ be a reduced integral noetherian excellent $QQ$-scheme and let $D\in\operatorname{\mathbf{CDiv}}_{\mathbb{Q}}X$ be nef. A **determination** of $D$ is a modification $f:Y\to X$ on which the b-divisor $D$ is represented by a Cartier divisor $D(Y)$; its **center** is the locus where $D$ is not Cartier on $X$.

**Nef Cartier b-divisor determination conjecture.** If $D\in\operatorname{\mathbf{CDiv}}_{\mathbb{Q}}X$ is nef, then there exists a determination of $D$ with center equal to the Cartier locus of $f$.

This conjecture seeks a geometric determination with the smallest possible center for nef Cartier b-divisors. The supplied text does not state whether it has been resolved.

record.title: Mirzakhani's conjecture on higher-rank affine invariant submanifolds
record.statement: Let $\mathcal{N}$ be a higher-rank affine invariant submanifold of a stratum of translation surfaces. A translation surface is **not primitive** if it covers a quadratic differential of lower genus. **Mirzakhani's conjecture.** Every higher-rank affine invariant submanifold $\mathcal{N}$ is either a stratum or is not primitive, in the sense that every translation surface in it covers a quadratic differential of lower genus. In the non-primitive case, $\mathcal{N}$ should arise from a covering construction, but it remains open to determine exactly which such constructions are possible.

record.title: Generic maximality conjecture for moving curve ideal generators
record.statement: For $d\geq 1$, let $\mathbb{V}_d$ be the set of triples of degree-$d$ homogeneous polynomials defining proper parametrizations. Let $\mathbb{W}_d$ be the open subset of $\mathbb{V}_d$ parametrizing curves with $\mu=\lfloor d/2\rfloor$ and whose singular points are all ordinary double points. **Generic maximality conjecture.** The invariant $n_0({\mathcal K})$ is constant on $\mathbb{W}_d$ and attains its maximal value on $\mathbb{V}_d$ in this component. This claim concerns the generic case, where the moving curve ideal is expected to have the largest value of $n_0$.

record.title: Refined maximum choice number conjecture for graphs of prescribed order and chromatic number
record.statement:
Let $n\geq k\geq 2$. For a graph $G$, write $\alpha(G)$ for its independence number, $\chi(G)$ for its chromatic number, and $\operatorname{ch}(G)$ for its choice number. **Refined maximum choice number conjecture.** There exists a graph $G_{n,k}$ such that:

- $G_{n,k}$ is a complete $k$-partite graph on $n$ vertices;
- $\alpha(G_{n,k})=\left\lceil\frac{n}{k}\right\rceil$;
- every $k$-chromatic graph $G$ on at most $n$ vertices satisfies
 
$$
\operatorname{ch}(G)\leq \operatorname{ch}(G_{n,k}).
$$

This refines the bounded-order conjecture by removing the requirement that the order be an integer multiple of the chromatic number. Its general validity is left open in the source.
record.source_name: Jonathan A. Noel, “Choosability of Graphs with Bounded Order: Ohba's Conjecture and Beyond”, arXiv:1309.0225 (2013).

record.title: The Delta-squared conjecture for weighted graph labeling
record.statement:
Let $(G,H)$ be a pair of graphs with $H\subset G$. Let $\operatorname{Span}(G,H)$ denote the minimum span of a $(G,H)$-labeling, and write $\Delta=\Delta(H)$ and $\Delta(G)$ for the respective maximum degrees. **Weighted Delta-squared conjecture.** If $\Delta\geq 2$ and $\Delta(G)\leq\Delta^2$, then

$$
\operatorname{Span}(G,H)\leq\Delta^2.
$$

This proposed extension is motivated by the similarities between $(G,H)$-labelings and $L(2,1)$-labelings; the source gives no resolution evidence.
record.source_name: Cole Franks, “Graph Labeling with Distance Conditions and the Delta Squared Conjecture”, arXiv:1309.0259 (2013).

record.title: Dokos–Dwyer–Jelinek–Sagan–Savage conjecture on inversion-Wilf equivalence
record.statement:
Let $\Pi$ and $\Pi'$ be sets of permutation patterns. For a permutation statistic $\operatorname{inv}$, define

$$
F^{\operatorname{inv}}_n(\Pi;q)=\sum_{\sigma\in\mathfrak{S}_n(\Pi)}q^{\operatorname{inv}(\sigma)}.
$$

The sets $\Pi$ and $\Pi'$ are **inversion-Wilf equivalent** if $F^{\operatorname{inv}}_n(\Pi;q)=F^{\operatorname{inv}}_n(\Pi';q)$ for all $n\geq 0$. Let $D_4$ act on permutation matrices, with $R_0,R_{180},r_{-1},r_1$ denoting the identity, the $180$-degree rotation, and reflections in lines of slopes $-1$ and $1$, respectively.

**Dokos et al.'s conjecture.** The sets $\Pi$ and $\Pi'$ are inversion-Wilf equivalent if and only if

$$
\Pi=f(\Pi')
$$

for some $f\in\{R_0,R_{180},r_{-1},r_1\}$.

These are precisely the evident equivalences preserving the inversion statistic under rotations and reflections of permutation matrices. The conjecture asserts that no other inversion-Wilf equivalences exist; its resolution is not specified in the source.
record.source_name: Wuttisak Trongsiriwat, “Permutation Statistics and Multiple Pattern Avoidance”, arXiv:1309.3028 (2013).

record.title: Poonen's power-set conjecture for separating families
record.statement:
Let $mathcal A$ be a separating union-closed family. A family is a **power set** if it consists of all subsets of some universe, and an element is **abundant** if it appears in more than half of the member-sets.

**Poonen's conjecture.** Unless $mathcal A$ is a power set, it contains an element that appears in strictly more than half of its member-sets.

Power sets show why the strict inequality is necessary: their maximum frequency can be exactly half the family size. The source gives no resolution.
record.source_name: Henning Bruhn and Oliver Schaudt, “The journey of the union-closed sets conjecture”, arXiv:1309.3297 (2013).

record.title: The connected-heavy-edge conjecture for $T_5$-factors
record.statement:
Let $M$ be a standard multigraph on $n$ vertices, where $n$ is divisible by $3$. Let $\delta(M)$ denote its minimum degree, let $H_M$ be its heavy-edge graph, and let a **$T_5$-factor** mean a factor consisting of copies of $T_5$. The **connected-heavy-edge conjecture** asserts that if

$$
\delta(M)\ge \frac{4}{3}n-1
$$

and $H_M$ is connected, then $M$ has a $T_5$-factor.
The conjecture is presented as a possible strengthening suggested by an extremal example; the supplied text does not state that it has been proved or disproved.

record.title: The hypersphere divisibility conjecture for preon constituents
record.statement: Let a preon be a constituent of a superordinate preon, and let the constituent structure use a number of hyperspheres. Let the **kissing number** of a space be the maximum number of nonoverlapping unit hyperspheres tangent to a given unit hypersphere in that space. **Hypersphere divisibility conjecture.** The number of hyperspheres used as constituents of a superordinate preon must divide the kissing number of the space in which they live. This is presented as the paper's second conjecture, linking its speculative preon configurations to geometric kissing-number constraints. No resolution or supporting theorem is supplied in the source.

record.title: Polynomial-time computation of the hull number of atomistic lattices
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{L}$ be an atomistic lattice with maximum element $\mathbf{1}$ and set of atoms $A(\mathcal{L})$. For a subset $H\subseteq A(\mathcal{L})$, write $\bigvee H$ for its join.

**Atomistic-lattice hull-number conjecture.** The minimum size of a subset $H\subseteq A(\mathcal{L})$ such that

$$
\bigvee H=\mathbf{1}
$$

can be computed in polynomial time.

The preceding proposition gives a quasi-polynomial-time algorithm by bounding the hull number in terms of the logarithm of the lattice size, assuming joins can be computed in polynomial time. The conjecture generalizes the corresponding question for linear extension graphs and would provide a polynomial-time method for this lattice optimization problem.
record.source_name: Marie Albenque and Kolja Knauer, “Convexity in partial cubes: the hull number”, arXiv:1309.5724 (2015).

record.title: The uniqueness and non-degeneracy conjecture for the lowest band-function minimum
record.statement: Let $\zeta_{1}(\tau)$ be the lowest band function associated with the three-dimensional magnetic Hamiltonian with axisymmetric potential. The preceding analysis shows that $\zeta_{1}$ is non-increasing on $(-\infty,0)$, and numerical simulations suggest that $\zeta_{2}(\tau)-3\zeta_{1}(\tau)>0$ for $\tau>0$. **Uniqueness and non-degeneracy conjecture.** The band function $\tau\mapsto\zeta_{1}(\tau)$ has a unique and non-degenerate minimum. This conjecture would determine the structure of the lowest band function and its critical points, building on the known monotonicity for negative $\tau$ and the observed positivity of the spectral gap; its resolution is not established here.

record.title: Benson–Carlson conjecture on free sphere-product actions
record.statement:
For a finite group $G$, define

$$
h(G)=\min\{s\mid G\text{ acts freely on }\mathbb{S}^{n_1}\times\cdots\times\mathbb{S}^{n_s}\},
$$

and

$$
r(G)=\max\{t\mid (\mathbb{Z}/p)^t\leq G\text{ for some prime }p\}.
$$

**Benson–Carlson conjecture.** One has $h(G)=r(G)$ for each finite group $G$.
This conjecture relates the minimum number of sphere factors needed for a free action to the largest elementary abelian subgroup rank of the group. The source presents it as an extension of Smith's theorem to products of spheres; no resolution is supplied here.
record.source_name: Mahender Singh, “Free 2-rank of symmetry of products of Milnor manifolds”, arXiv:1309.7475 (2013).

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of September 2013). “A lens space $L_p^{2n-1}$ is an odd dimensional spherical space form obtained as the quotient of the standard $\mathbb{Z}/p$ action on $\mathbb{S}^{2n-1}$.”

record.title: Wang's 2-factor embedding conjecture for bipartite graphs
record.statement:
Let $G[U,V]$ and $H$ be balanced bipartite graphs on $2n$ vertices. Write $\delta_U$ and $\delta_V$ for the minimum degrees of vertices in $U$ and $V$ in $G$, respectively, and let $\Delta(H)$ denote the maximum degree of $H$. **Wang's conjecture.** If

$$
\delta_U+\delta_V\geq n+2
$$

and

$$
\Delta(H)\leq 2,
$$

then $H\subseteq G$. This would provide an analogue of the matching result for tiling with $K_{2,2}$; the source gives no resolution of the conjecture.

record.title: The generalized Fermat equation conjecture for prime exponents and prime-power gcd
record.statement:
Let $A,B,C,D,n\in\mathbb{Z}_{+}$ with $n\geq3$, and suppose

$$
A+B=C,\qquad ABC=D^n.
$$

Assume that $\gcd(A,B,C)=p^k$, where $p$ is an odd prime and $k\in\mathbb{Z}_{+}$. **Generalized Fermat equation conjecture.** If $n\geq3$ is prime and $p\not\equiv1\pmod{2n}$, then the system has no positive integer solutions. This conjecture extends the proved cases $n=3$ and $n=5$ discussed in the paper; the stated condition excludes primes $p\equiv1\pmod{2n}$, for which the authors construct solutions in certain cases.
record.source_name: Tianxin Cai, Deyi Chen and Yong Zhang, “A New Generalization of Fermat's Last Theorem”, arXiv:1310.0897 (2014).

record.title: The tree-width computation problem for switch cographs
record.statement: A **switch cograph** is a graph in the class discussed above, obtained through the switch-cograph decomposition; let its tree-width be the minimum width of a tree decomposition of the graph. **Tree-width conjecture.** The problem of computing the tree-width of a switch cograph is NP-complete. The tree-width of switch cographs is not bounded, and the computational complexity of determining it is left open in the source.

record.title: The maximum-degree conjecture for critical graphs
record.statement:
A graph is **critical** with tree-depth $k$ if its tree-depth is $k$ and every proper minor has smaller tree-depth. The maximum degree of a graph $G$ is denoted by $\delta(G)$.

**The maximum-degree conjecture.** Every critical graph with tree-depth $k$ has maximum degree at most

$$
k-1.
$$

The bound is proved for the class of $1$-unique critical graphs, and several classes of critical graphs are known to lie in that class. Whether every critical graph satisfies the bound remains open.

record.title: Rigidity conjecture for Lyapunov-exponent maximizers on the two-torus
record.statement: Let $f$ be a $C^2$ volume-preserving Anosov diffeomorphism of $\mathbb{T}^2$, and let $\Lambda:\operatorname{Diff}^2_m(\mathbb{T}^2)\to\mathbb{R}$ be the functional defined in the source. **Rigidity conjecture.** If $f$ is a local maximum for $\Lambda$, then $f$ is $C^1$ conjugate to a linear toral automorphism. This is a rigidity statement for local maximizers of a Lyapunov-exponent functional; the supplied text gives no evidence that it has been proved or disproved.

record.title: Rankin's set conjecture for the maximal density of geometric-progression-free sets
record.statement:
Let $G^*_3$ denote Rankin's geometric-progression-free set, and let $d(G^*_3)$ be its density. Let $alpha$ be the supremum of the densities of geometric-progression-free sets that possess a density.

**Rankin's set conjecture.** Rankin's set $G^*_3$ has the largest possible density among geometric-progression-free sets which have a density, so

$$
\alpha=d(G^*_3).
$$

The paper establishes an effective method for computing the maximal upper density of sets avoiding three-term geometric progressions, but the precise value of $\alpha$ remains open. This conjecture is stronger than the question of whether $\alpha$ is strictly smaller than the corresponding maximal upper density.

record.title: Unbounded separation between orbital chromatic and chromatic roots
record.statement:
Let $N>0$. A graph $\Gamma$ has chromatic polynomial $P_{\Gamma}(x)$, and let $G$ be an automorphism group of $\Gamma$. The orbital chromatic polynomial $OP_{\Gamma,G}(x)$ is the polynomial associated with the action of $G$ on $\Gamma$.

**Unbounded separation conjecture.** For any $N>0$, there exists a graph $\Gamma$ and automorphism group $G$ of $\Gamma$ for which $OP_{\Gamma,G}(x)$ has a root at least $N$ larger than the largest real root of $P_{\Gamma}(x)$.

This conjecture asks whether orbital chromatic roots can lie arbitrarily far to the right of the largest real chromatic root. The paper notes that orbital chromatic roots can exceed chromatic roots, but gives no resolution of whether their separation is unbounded.
record.source_name: Dae Hyun Kim, Alexander H. Mun and Mohamed Omar, “Chromatic Bounds On Orbital Chromatic Roots”, arXiv:1310.3792 (2014).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1310.3792

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2013).

record.title: Beck's conjecture for annihilating ideal-graphs of commutative rings
record.statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring with unity. Define the annihilating ideal-graph $\mathbb{AG}(R)$ to have as vertices the nonzero ideals $I$ with nonzero annihilator, meaning that there is a nonzero ideal $J$ such that $IJ=(0)$; distinct vertices $I$ and $J$ are adjacent precisely when $IJ=(0)$. Write $\chi(\mathbb{AG}(R))$ for its chromatic number and $\operatorname{Clique}(\mathbb{AG}(R))$ for its clique number.

**Beck's conjecture.** For every commutative ring $R$ with unity,

$$
\chi(\mathbb{AG}(R))=\operatorname{Clique}(\mathbb{AG}(R)).
$$

The paper states this conjecture as the ring-theoretic claim motivating its extension to multiplicative lattices. The abstract reports a counterexample for multiplicative lattices, while also stating that the conjecture holds for reduced multiplicative lattices; the status of the original ring formulation is not resolved in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Vinayak Joshi and Sachin Sarode, “Beck's Conjecture For Multiplicative Lattices”, arXiv:1310.4594 (2013).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1310.4594

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2013).

record.title: Generalized Cranston–Kim conjecture for powers of graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a simple connected graph with maximum degree $\Delta\geq 3$. For $k\in\mathbb{N}^*$, let $G^k$ be the graph obtained by joining vertices at distance at most $k$, and define

$$
D(k,\Delta)=\Delta\sum_{i=1}^{k}(\Delta-1)^{i-1}=\Delta\frac{(\Delta-1)^k-1}{\Delta-2}.
$$

A **Moore graph** is a graph on $\Delta^2+1$ vertices whose square is a clique. **Generalized Cranston–Kim conjecture.** For any $k\in\mathbb{N}^*$, except for Moore graphs when $k=2$, the $k$th power $G^k$ is $(D(k,\Delta)-1)$-choosable. The paper proves this assertion for $k\geq 3$, and the $k=2$ case was proved subsequently, so the conjecture is solved.
record.source_name: Marthe Bonamy and Nicolas Bousquet, “Brooks' theorem on powers of graphs”, arXiv:1310.5493 (2013).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1310.5493

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of October 2013); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “solved”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

record.title: Stronger finite-exception conjecture for choosability of graph powers
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a simple connected graph with maximum degree $\Delta\geq 3$. For $k\in\mathbb{N}^*$, let $G^k$ be the graph obtained by joining vertices at distance at most $k$, and define

$$
D(k,\Delta)=\Delta\sum_{i=1}^{k}(\Delta-1)^{i-1}=\Delta\frac{(\Delta-1)^k-1}{\Delta-2}.
$$

**Stronger finite-exception conjecture.** For any $k\in\mathbb{N}^*$, except for a finite number of graphs, the $k$th power $G^k$ is $(D(k,\Delta)+1-k)$-choosable. This is posed as a stronger generalization of the square-choosability conjecture, and the source does not report a resolution.
record.source_name: Marthe Bonamy and Nicolas Bousquet, “Brooks' theorem on powers of graphs”, arXiv:1310.5493 (2013).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1310.5493

record.title: The sharp symmetry-rank conjecture for cyclic fundamental groups
record.statement:
Let $M^{2m-1}$ be a closed Riemannian manifold with positive sectional curvature. Let $q$ denote the smallest prime divisor of $m$, and let an $r$-torus act effectively and isometrically on $M$. **Sharp cyclicity conjecture.** If

$$
r \geq \frac{m}{q}+1,
$$

then $\pi_1(M)$ is cyclic. This conjecture would give a sharp obstruction to non-cyclic fundamental groups under a sufficiently large torus symmetry rank; the bound is motivated by spherical space-form examples, which show that the corresponding threshold cannot generally be lowered.
record.source_name: Lee Kennard, “Fundamental groups of manifolds with positive sectional curvature and torus symmetry”, arXiv:1310.7251 (2015).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1310.7251

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2013).

record.title: The majority out-dominating number conjecture for complete bipartite graphs
record.statement:
Let $K_{r,s}$ be a complete bipartite graph with $r\leq s$, and let $DOM^{+}_m(K_{r,s})$ denote its majority out-dominating number. Assume that $DOM^{+}_m(K_{r,s})\neq1$. 

**Majority out-dominating number conjecture.**

$$
DOM^{+}_m(K_{r,s}) = \begin{cases} 2 & \text{if } s\leq r+2,\\ \left\lceil\frac{s-r}{2}\right\rceil & \text{otherwise.}\end{cases}
$$

The preceding results determine exactly when this parameter equals $1$, but the general value for complete bipartite graphs is described as difficult to find. The displayed formula is proposed as the conjectured value in all remaining cases; its resolution is not indicated in the source.
record.source_name: Karam Ebadi, Martín Manrique, Reza Jafary and J. Joseline Manora, “Majority out-dominating sets in digraphs”, arXiv:1311.0479 (2013).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1311.0479

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2013).

record.title: Symmetric-norm minimizer conjecture for slow entropy
record.statement:
Let $\chi_i$ be the linear forms associated with a Cartan action, and let $q$ range over the norms occurring in the minimization problem for the slow-entropy estimate. The minimum in the relevant regulator minimization problem should be attained at

$$
q(x)=\max_i\lvert\chi_i\cdot x\rvert.
$$

This conjecture would identify the symmetric candidate suggested by low-dimensional computations and symmetry arguments, thereby determining the minimizer and potentially the exact constant in the slow-entropy bounds. The paper does not provide a proof.
record.source_name: Anatole Katok, Svetlana Katok and Federico Rodriguez Hertz, “The Fried average entropy and slow entropy for actions of higher rank abelian groups”, arXiv:1311.0927 (2014).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1311.0927

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2013).

record.title: Cranston–Kim conjecture on list coloring squares of graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected graph with maximum degree $\Delta\ge 3$. Let $G^2$ be its square, and let $\chi_{\ell}(G^2)$ denote the list chromatic number of $G^2$. A **Moore graph** is a $\Delta$-regular graph on $\Delta^2+1$ vertices such that $G^2=K_{\Delta^2+1}$.

**Cranston–Kim conjecture.** If $G$ is not a Moore graph, then

$$
\chi_{\ell}(G^2)\le \Delta^2-1.
$$

The source states that Cranston and Kim proved the conjecture for $\Delta=3$, while Bonamy and Bousquet proved the full claim in the more general setting of online list coloring.
record.source_name: Daniel W. Cranston and Landon Rabern, “Painting Squares in Δ^2-1 Shades”, arXiv:1311.1251 (2014).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1311.1251

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of November 2013). “This was proved by Bonamy and Bousquet in the more general context of online list coloring.”

record.title: Optimal exterior-barrier length conjecture for the unit square
record.statement:
Let an **exterior barrier** for the unit square be a barrier lying outside the square, and call a barrier **optimal** if it has minimum length among barriers of the relevant type.

**Exterior-barrier length conjecture.** The length of an optimal exterior barrier for the unit square is $3$.

The paper says this is suggested by the leftmost barrier in its Figure 1. It is presented as an open conjecture, alongside the question of obtaining nontrivial lower bounds for unrestricted barriers.
record.source_name: Adrian Dumitrescu and Minghui Jiang, “The opaque square”, arXiv:1311.3323 (2013).

record.title: Engbers–Galvin conjecture on independent sets of fixed size
record.statement:
Let $G$ be an $n$-vertex graph with minimum degree at least $b4$, and let $i_t(G)$ denote the number of independent sets of size $t$ in $G$. Assume $t\geq 3$ and $\delta\leq n/2$.

**Engbers–Galvin conjecture.** The complete bipartite graph $K_{\delta,n-\delta}$ maximizes $i_t(G)$ over all $n$-vertex graphs with minimum degree at least $\delta$.

This is a fixed-size strengthening of Galvin's conjecture on the total number of independent sets. The conjecture was proved in the paper, so it is no longer open.
record.source_name: Wenying Gan, Po-Shen Loh and Benny Sudakov, “Maximizing the number of independent sets of a fixed size”, arXiv:1311.4147 (2014).
